subject: PayCore discovery — pilot economics & budget anchors
messages:
From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Aisha Khan <aisha.khan@paycore.com>, Michael Tran <michael.tran@paycore.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 26 May 2026 11:07:00 -0400
Subject: PayCore discovery — pilot economics & budget anchors

Thanks again for your time today — quick recap so we’re all aligned and can move to a concrete pilot SOW. Notes below are drawn from our call (Grace) + follow-ups from Marissa and Jonas.

Key pain points you described
- Token spend unpredictability: spikes during peak settlement windows are driving 3–4x monthly variance.
- Latency sensitivity: under 200ms p95 for customer-facing scoring calls is a hard constraint.
- Ops complexity: existing infra struggles with high-concurrency bursts; team prefers managed inference.

Goals for a pilot / success criteria
- Demonstrate 40–60% per-token cost reduction vs your current managed endpoint for the same quality (meaning same model family + prompts).
- Hold p95 latency <= 250ms under realistic concurrency during a 2–3 week pilot load test.
- Operational playbook: rollout plan for caching/prefixing and autoscaling rules.

Initial TCO levers we discussed (high level)
- Continuous batching (keeps latency but increases utilization) + request shaping for peak windows.
- Prefix/KV cache for repeated session tokens (expected 20–35% token savings on conversational flows).
- Model variant routing: quantized 4-bit variant for background scoring, full-fp32 for critical flows.
- Reserved (Dedicated) capacity option for steady-state to reduce per-token unit cost vs pure hosted.

Immediate asks / next steps (can you confirm by EOD Thursday?)
1) Approx monthly active tokens (we discussed 200M–400M) and peak concurrent requests (your ops estimate of ~650 qps during settlement).
2) Target pilot budget range / maximum acceptable pilot spend (you mentioned looking for a low-risk POC).
3) Procurement timeline: any PO or legal gating we should plan for?

Attached: draft pilot scope (paycore_pilot_scope_draft.pdf), rough TCO model (paycore_rough_tco_model.xlsx), and the usage snapshot you shared consolidated into a CSV (paycore_usage_snapshot.csv).

Calendaring: If those asks look right, propose a 30–45 minute follow-up next Wed to align SOW and calendar run dates.

Thanks — Grace

--

From: Aisha Khan <aisha.khan@paycore.com>

Cc: Michael Tran <michael.tran@paycore.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 26 May 2026 14:32:00 +0000
Subject: Re: PayCore discovery — pilot economics & budget anchors

Grace — thanks for the crisp recap, super helpful. Quick answers inline: 

1) Monthly tokens: current average ~280M tokens/month. During settlement windows we see ~3.5x uplift for ~2 hours/day; peak qps estimate is 620–700 depending on batch windows. (See attached CSV — I pulled the last 90 days.)
2) Pilot budget: to get internal approvals we need to cap the pilot at $50k committed spend (all-in) or it gets escalated up to procurement and will take longer. If Redwood can scope a focused 2-week POC that demonstrates the majority of savings within that number, we can greenlight.
3) Procurement: we have a standard SOW PO process. If the pilot ask is <= $50k I can sign with VP approval in ~5 business days; above that will require procurement involvement and ~3 weeks.

Two clarifications from our side:
- We want the pilot to include a clear pass/fail gating around per-token unit economics and an ops handoff checklist.
- Can you propose the minimal pilot footprint (nodes, expected qps) that fits the budget and still gives meaningful data?

Happy to take that offline — propose Thu 11am PT to go over a tightened scope.

—Aisha
Aisha Khan
Head of ML Infrastructure
PayCore

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Aisha Khan <aisha.khan@paycore.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 27 May 2026 08:41:00 -0700
Subject: Re: PayCore discovery — pilot economics & budget anchors

Aisha — thanks for the quick context and the budget cap — that helps a lot. A few notes from pricing side and a proposed compressed pilot: 

Compressed pilot (designed to hit the $50k cap)
- Duration: 2 weeks (10 business days) with a 48–72 hour concentrated load test at target concurrency.
- Footprint: 4 dedicated GPU workers (quantized variant) + 1 hot worker for unquantized critical calls; autoscaling disabled during concentrated load test to capture steady-state economics.
- Observability: full token/latency breakdowns, trace sampling, and ops runbook delivery.
- Expected measurable outcomes: token savings from KV cache + batching simulated from a replay of 30 days (replay + live spike test).

Commercial options
- Pilot (no long-term commitment) — $50k fixed for two-week run and analysis; includes rollout playbook.
- Pilot + optional 12-month reserved capacity credit — if you convert within 30 days we can apply a usage credit equal to 25% of the pilot fee toward the first month of reserved capacity.

If that tradeoff sounds sensible I’ll draft a one-page SOW and send it over today. Grace / Jonas — I’ll need the minimal node sizing and expected replay dataset size to finalize the footprint. Jonas, can you confirm the replay approach and whether the 30-day sampling is sufficient to model settlement spikes?

Thanks — Marissa
Senior Account Exec | Redwood Inference
